note: Every row here is something a reader must not silently assume. Blank cells are intentional.

flags.item: Standings render without a text header row
flags.finding: The NFL.com division standings table displayed no header text, and the field order does not match the page legend order. Division record and conference record are named in the legend but their displayed position could not be confirmed; four further middle fields are also unidentified. Six of sixteen displayed fields were therefore not transcribed.
flags.impact: Division and conference detail is unavailable on this site. Retained fields were the ones confirmable by arithmetic.

flags.item: Blank game status for 17 of 20 listed players
flags.finding: The official listing shows a blank 'Game Status' for most players while still listing practice participation. The page does not explain, row by row, whether blank means available.
flags.impact: No player is treated as available or unavailable beyond the two Out and one Questionable entries.

flags.item: No depth chart or snap count retrieved
flags.finding: NFL.com's depth-chart address returned a 404 to the reader. No published starter list and no snap share was obtained.
flags.impact: The starter-versus-backup and second/third-string requirement is documented but NOT measured. Every depth field is blank.

flags.item: Home-field adjustment is an assumption
flags.finding: A single 2.0-point home adjustment is applied to all 14 fixtures, including the Munich international game which is not a true home game for either club.
flags.impact: Every originated spread inherits this assumption. No official NFL home-field value was retrieved.

flags.item: No market price exists in the record
flags.finding: No sportsbook line, price, limit or hold for these NFL markets was retrieved, so ROI, CLV and break-even comparisons are blank.
flags.impact: No originated number is claimed to beat the market.

flags.item: Source-use restriction
flags.finding: NFL.com terms 1.3 permit individual non-commercial informational use and prohibit systematic retrieval to compile a collection without written consent.
flags.impact: No dataset is released, nothing is automated against NFL.com, and the site is a frozen attributed note.

flags.item: Single-source values
flags.finding: Every number in this section comes from one retrieved page. Arithmetic re-derivation catches contradictions, not a wrong page.
flags.impact: All values are labelled single-source. A two-source rule is proposed (S10).

flags.item: Five of ten team correlations are not independent evidence
flags.finding: Net points, wins and the record-versus-expectation residual share inputs by construction. Those pairs are labelled on the correlation page rather than removed.
flags.impact: Only five pairs are presented as exploratory evidence.

flags.item: One partial season and one game of injury data
flags.finding: The NFL origination dataset contains 20 Thursday Nov 12 player rows. A separate availability desk in this repository contains a 326-row Week 10 snapshot for 28 clubs, captured 2026-11-13. The official live page opening chunk re-read on 2026-11-14 shows Sunday Nov 15 injury sections too; remaining chunks and the 326-row snapshot were not re-audited on 2026-11-14, so the snapshot is not claimed to be current.
flags.impact: No forward predictive claim is made and coverage fails its gate.

flags.item: Game results were deliberately not transcribed
flags.finding: The score pages rendered some finals as 'Hidden Score' in the reader. Rather than guess, no game-level results were stored, so no historical grading is offered.
flags.impact: No backtest exists. This is a coverage decision, not an oversight.

flags.item: Two-source rule not met
flags.finding: No value here is confirmed by an independent second official source.
flags.impact: Confidence is limited to what one official page supports.

flags.item: NBA section retained alongside NFL
flags.finding: The repository already contained a completed NBA audit and rental research. The NFL section becomes the landing page; the earlier pages remain reachable and keep their own limits.
flags.impact: Nothing from the earlier work was deleted or relabelled as NFL data.

flags.item: A completed game's result is printed, so 'no result exists' is no longer true
flags.finding: The 2026-11-12 register recorded that score pages rendered only 'Hidden Score', so no result was transcribed. On 2026-11-13 the schedule page prints 'Commanders 24, Giants 21, FINAL' in the fixture link text while still printing 'Hidden Score' in both score banners. The publisher contradicts itself on one page.
flags.impact: The frozen snapshot keeps no result, as recorded. The re-check page quotes both strings and records 24-21 only because it is the one reading consistent with the same day's standings arithmetic. No model is scored on it.

flags.item: Two clubs' records moved after the snapshot date
flags.finding: WAS was 2-5-1 with 172 PF / 202 PA on 2026-11-12 and is 3-5-1 with 196 PF / 223 PA on 2026-11-13. NYG moved the other way, 5-2-1 / 182 / 172 to 5-3-1 / 203 / 196. The deltas are a consistent 24-21 result. 30 of 32 rows are unchanged. Rechecked 2026-11-14 against all 32 rendered official club rows (W/L/T/PF/PA): the same 30 rows match and WAS/NYG remain the only two differences; the frozen snapshot was not changed.
flags.impact: The published table is a 2026-11-12 snapshot and says so. A reader comparing it with today's page will see a difference; the re-check page lists all 32 rows side by side so nothing looks silently stale.

flags.item: League depth-chart path still returns no chart; one club path returns 404
flags.finding: https://www.nfl.com/teams/depth-chart serves no league-wide chart, and https://www.nfl.com/teams/new-england-patriots/depth-chart returned a rendered '404 - Flag on the Play.' page on 2026-11-13.
flags.impact: No starter/backup ordering can be cited from the league site, so the second-, third- and fourth-string requirement stays unmet. Club-site chains remain the only official route and are not uniform.

flags.item: Two suggestion registers use different identifiers for the same work
flags.finding: research/nfl/decisions.json ranks ten suggestions as S01-S10; research/nfl-suggestions.json lists twelve as SU-01-SU-12 and is rendered on the sub-site's own Suggestions page. Depth charts are S02 in one and SU-03 plus SU-07 in the other.
flags.impact: Neither register is deleted. A published crosswalk maps each S-id to its SU-ids so a reviewer can follow either, and the reviewer is asked to adopt one register.

flags.item: Validation gates are a declared matrix, not executed tests
flags.finding: nfl_origination/engine.py assigns each candidate strategy a gate string. G01 and G02 are marked pass for snapshot-based candidates and G10 is open for all eight. No statistical test is executed whose outcome could flip a gate; a test asserts the matrix contains the assigned strings.
flags.impact: The page wording is accurate about the matrix, but a reader could infer the gates were run. No strategy is qualified either way, and the empty leaderboard is unaffected.

flags.item: No-information baseline is a 50% forecast, and the baseline rate is not stated
flags.finding: The published Brier comparison sets the model's 0.1575 against 0.25, the Brier score of a flat 50% forecast, across 32 clubs. The unconditional home-win rate in this snapshot is not 50% and the page does not state which rate the reference used.
flags.impact: The direction of the comparison is not in doubt. The reference is under-specified and is not a market comparison, and it is labelled accordingly.

flags.item: An originated line is shown for a fixture that has since kicked off
flags.finding: W10-01 (WAS at NYG, 2026-11-12 20:15 ET) carries an originated spread and total on the line origination page as of 2026-11-13. The gate table marks temporal integrity G02 as a blanket pass for the originated lines.
flags.impact: G02 remains a pass for the thirteen fixtures still unplayed. The retrospective row is labelled, and no result is used to score it.

flags.item: Page metadata describes every NFL page as NBA research
flags.finding: The page template in scripts/build_site.py hard-codes the description 'OWN7 NBA research: source-linked observations, exploratory models...' for all canonical pages, including the NFL landing page and every NFL sub-page.
flags.impact: Search engines and link previews mislabel the NFL section. Fixed by deriving the description per page.

flags.item: Page and question counts were typed as prose and had drifted
flags.finding: The landing page called the origination section eleven pages when it publishes twelve, and four rendered surfaces said 'fourteen questions' while the register holds fifteen. The navigation badge read 10 open items beside a twelve-row register without saying which it counted.
flags.impact: Counts are now derived from the data at build time and a test fails if a rendered count disagrees with its register. The badge states that it counts open items.

flags.item: Week 10 injury tables disagree across the repository's four desk files
flags.finding: availability desk: 326 rows, 28 clubs; assurance desk: 276 rows, 26 clubs, no BAL or LAC; origination desk: 210 rows, no LAR, practice codes DNP/Limited/Full; legacy file: 20 rows, WAS and NYG only, team nicknames. On the 276 players the assurance and availability desks share, the comparison found 19 injury, 19 game-status and 72 practice differences before practice labels were normalised.
flags.impact: Any one desk table alone would mislead. The official eight-chunk page is the reference; chunk 0 (50 rows) was matched field by field on 2026-11-17.

flags.item: Kerby Joseph practice status conflicts between the availability desk and the live page
flags.finding: Availability desk: Full Participation in Practice, Out. Live official page read 2026-11-17 (Detroit at New England, Sunday 15 Nov): Did Not Participate In Practice, Out. The game status agrees.
flags.impact: Practice-level evidence for this player is not reliable until the desk is corrected from the official page.

flags.item: Lions game status is blank in the assurance and origination desks
flags.finding: Kerby Joseph, Cade Mays and D.J. Reed are listed Out on the live official page (2026-11-17). The assurance and origination desks leave game status blank for all three.
flags.impact: Blank cells must not be read as available. The official page is the source for the correction.

flags.item: Week 10 final scores are not in the verified results feed
flags.finding: nfl-results/data/games-2026-w1-9.csv covers Weeks 1 to 9 (136 rows, retrieved 2026-11-14). Thirteen Week 10 finals printed on nfl.com/schedules on 2026-11-17 are not in the feed.
flags.impact: Results-based tests, leaderboard rows and the register's results gate run on Weeks 1 to 9 only.

flags.item: Chargers at Ravens (16 Nov) final score is not confirmed
flags.finding: The official schedule read on 2026-11-17 shows the game on Monday 16 Nov at 8:15 PM ET with no score printed. Thirteen of fourteen Week 10 games show Final.
flags.impact: The Week 10 result count is 13 of 14 until the official game page is read and linked.

flags.item: Week 10 venue notes are almost empty
flags.finding: Only one of the fourteen rows in nfl/origination/data/games-2026-w10.csv has a venue note. The others are blank, not inferred.
flags.impact: Venue-based features cannot be built. Each venue must be transcribed from the official game-centre page.

flags.item: Row-level NFL data is committed while the NFL.com terms restrict systematic retrieval
flags.finding: 832 injury rows across the four Week 10 desk tables are committed. NFL.com Terms §1.3 (read 2026-11-17, updated 16 May 2024) limits use to personal, non-commercial informational purposes and bars systematic retrieval without written consent. The README release wording was not re-read this session.
flags.impact: Public release of row-level data and scheduled capture need a rights decision (register decisions D1 and D3) before they continue.

flags.item: A backtest row is published on the results leaderboard
flags.finding: nfl-results-leaderboard.html shows a spread backtest record of 120 bets, 77 wins to 43 losses, although the pre-registration rule forbids backtest numbers on a leaderboard.
flags.impact: The row is retained and flagged, not removed or rebuilt in this session. It is excluded from every ranking claim in the register.

flags.item: The brief's multi-player depth count does not reproduce
flags.finding: The brief states 149 multi-player slots. Recomputed from the committed files: 134 rank-1 groups with more than one player in the availability desk, 22 in the four bye clubs, 156 combined. Offence and defence only: 155 combined. The definition is not settled.
flags.impact: Depth-group counts must not be quoted as 149 until the owner confirms the definition.

flags.item: Price-data policy differs between desks
flags.finding: The pricing desk holds Pro-Football-Reference closing-price observations. The lifecycle desk keeps market values blank under its rights policy. No single written policy applies to both.
flags.impact: No market-relative result, residual or ROI can be published until the owner records one policy (register decision D2).

flags.item: Lions Week 10 designations differ between the desk captures and the official read
flags.finding: Official page read 2026-11-17: Kerby Joseph (Knee, DNP, Out), Cade Mays (Ankle, DNP, Out), D.J. Reed (Hip, DNP, Out), Amon-Ra St. Brown (Rib, LP, Questionable), Sione Vaki (Ankle, LP, Questionable). The availability desk capture (2026-11-13) shows Joseph as Full Participation, and St. Brown and Vaki with no injury and no game status; Vaki is DNP. Published as a dated delta on the landing page; no capture was overwritten. The page prints no capture time, so the cause cannot be settled.
flags.impact: Three Out designations are confirmed by the official read. Practice and injury fields for the other rows depend on which capture is used.

flags.item: Three desks hold three different Week 10 injury row counts
flags.finding: The availability desk holds 326 rows, the assurance desk 276 rows (its build text says 276), and the research extract 20 rows. These are different scopes or captures of one official report. The brief's figures (254 and 279 rows) are not reproduced in the repository. No complete official recount was made this session; the page has eight chunks and one was read.
flags.impact: Row counts cannot be quoted as the league total until one complete official recount matches every row.

flags.item: Committed NFL row-level data conflicts with the repository's own rights gate
flags.finding: 64 NFL-named CSV files are committed and served by the public GitHub Pages site, including per-game and per-player rows (for example nfl-results/data/games-2026-w1-9.csv, 136 games). The rights gate RG10 states that nothing is released because NFL.com terms do not permit releasing a compiled dataset, and the README says no dataset is released. Both statements cannot hold.
flags.impact: Possible breach of NFL.com terms §1.3 by the public site. Not changed in this session: the brief requires a public/private split, but moving files breaks five desks. Owner decision needed.

flags.item: Scheduled capture of NFL.com conflicts with terms §1.3 unless written consent is obtained
flags.finding: The brief asks for daily scheduled capture of injury reports and depth pages from Wednesday to kickoff, with retained hashes. NFL.com terms §1.3 allow individual non-commercial informational use and prohibit systematic retrieval without express prior written consent. No scheduled job was added. The Week 10 Lions read was a single page read, not a scheduled job.
flags.impact: Scheduled capture is blocked until written consent or a licensed feed is in place.

flags.item: Identifiers cited in the brief are not in the repository
flags.finding: The brief cites verification IDs VR-04 to VR-26, VQ-05 to VQ-08, and rejection IDs SG-03 and SG-05. A repository-wide search on 2026-11-17 returned no match for any of them. Claims that rely on those IDs (for example Malik Willis on injured reserve, the Colts receiver trades, and the Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley depth rows) therefore cannot be traced here and are not published as verified.
flags.impact: Those items remain open. The owner should supply the register that defines the IDs.

flags.item: Removal-of-luck family size: 18 stated, 30 graded
flags.finding: The analysis states strategies_tested = 18 and a family-wise false-positive of 2.18% (1 − (1 − 0.001223)^18). The leaderboard tests 30 graded variants. Recomputed on 30, the family-wise figure is 3.60%. Both are below 5%, but the stated family is not the graded family.
flags.impact: The dashboard shows both figures. The owner should fix the family definition before the number is used for a decision.

flags.item: Other desks' leaderboards show hit-rate columns
flags.finding: Under the brief's rule that backtest numbers never appear on a leaderboard, the lifecycle leaderboard (2 hit-rate columns), the pricing leaderboard (5) and the market-desk leaderboard (1) still show hit-rate figures. Only the results leaderboard was corrected in this session, because those desks are owned by earlier sessions.
flags.impact: Leaderboard pages in those desks breach the stated rule until they are corrected.

flags.item: Results leaderboard showed backtest numbers; withheld from 2026-11-17
flags.finding: The results leaderboard ranked the originated spread board as provisional #1 and printed its hit rate (64.2%), interval, and q-value. The brief forbids backtest numbers on a leaderboard. The page now lists each variant as not ranked, with eligibility only; the figures remain on the skill page, labelled as backtest.
flags.impact: Corrected. No value in the analysis file was changed.

flags.item: Five open pull requests from stale parallel sessions were reconciled by takeover (four closed unmerged, one merged)
flags.finding: PRs #17, #27, #48, #50 and #51 belonged to sessions whose coordination claims were more than 60 hours old with no commits. The brief makes such tasks takeable. Review of each branch against main found: #51 (NFL competition lab, 16 pages, 59 tests) implements the brief's headline requirements with unique artifacts (deficiency matrix, decision record, 137-game feed) and was merged additively into main via this session's integration PR; #48 and #50 are two further independent implementations of the same eight lifecycle requirements that main already covers (nfl-lifecycle-3f5c, nfl-pricing, nfl-market-desk); #27 is an earlier decision desk superseded by the canonical decision pages and failing its browser checks at closure time; #17 records NBA-era source-health work whose workflow and script already exist on main. Branches remain in Git history and can be reopened as new PRs if the owner disagrees. (Flag registered as NF22 on the integration branch before main's NF22-NF31 range was seen; renumbered to NF40 on merge.)
flags.impact: Avoids publishing three-to-five overlapping price stores, leaderboards and demotion gates that would contradict each other on one site. The closure rationale is recorded here, on each PR, and in COORDINATION.md; nothing was deleted.
